# Introduction

The purpose of this code is to extract environmental data on extant species within our samples using the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS). Occurrence data will be limited to datasets that meet the following criteria:

**Criteria**

* **Geographic location**: Occurences must be from the mid-Atlantic ridge to US East Coast and from the equator to the Denmark Strait, excluding the Gulf of Mexico (see "watlclean.json", and https://www.arcgis.com/apps/mapviewer/index.html?layers=f3f5b13127704cd1a47d37bc5c86b620 )
* **Non-fossil occurences**: "basisOfRecord" cannot equal "FossilSpecimen
* Must contain non-N/A entries for the following columns:
  * decimalLatitude
  * decimalLongitude 
  * bathymetry"
  * sss (sea surface salinity)
  * sst (sea surface temperature)
  
For more information on OBIS data attributes, see: https://obis.org/data/access/ and https://manual.obis.org/darwin_core.html.

This code is based on the November 22, 2016 tutorial from OBIS: https://obis.org/2016/11/22/sorbycollection/ 

```{r Packages, echo=True, results='hide'}
#1library(taxizesoap)
library(robis)
#library(ggmap)
library(dplyr)
library(ncdf4)
library(raster)
library(stringr)
library(readr)

```

## Importing geometry

Use JSON file of Western Atlantic to filter OBIS records. Drawn in OBIS mapper, then data was downloaded and query geometry was saved as a json file. "Western Atlantic" was defined based on this GIS map (https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=f3f5b13127704cd1a47d37bc5c86b620#overview) and includes ocean from the mid-Atlantic ridge to US East Coast and from the equator to the Denmark Strait, excluding the Gulf of Mexico. 

```{r Importing geometry}
geom_json<- fromJSON("watlclean.json")
obis_clean_w_atl<- geom_json$geometry
```

## Importing taxonomic data

Importing data that is table of all taxa present in our samples, 
```{r Import raw data}
taxa_df_raw<- read_csv("mpwp_sp_010426.csv") # taxa present across all our samples
taxa_list<- as.list(taxa_df_raw$taxon_name) # list of taxa names
```

## Pre-processing taxonomic data
1) Determinging if taxon has OBIS record appending that column to the taxa dataframe
```{r Determine if OBIS records exist}

obis_yn<- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(taxa_df_raw))){ #go through taxa data
  taxa<- taxa_list[i] #for specific taxa
  occ<- occurrence(scientificname=taxa) #pull occurrence
  if (nrow(occ)==0){ #if length of occurrence record is zero
    obis_yn[i]= "No" #say no
  }
  else{
    obis_yn[i]= "Yes" #say yes
  }
}

```

2) Making column about whether there is a record in OBIS
```{r Make column about whether taxa is in OBIS}
taxa_df_raw$has_obis_rec <- c(obis_yn) 
```

3) Make a dataframe only of taxa that are in OBIS
```{r Make dataframe of OBIS taxa}
obis_taxa_df<- taxa_df_raw[taxa_df_raw$has_obis_rec == "Yes", ] #has "Yes" in the 'has_obis_rec' column
obis_taxa_list<- as.list(obis_taxa_df$taxon_name)
```

## Setting up a summary dataframe
Create a dataframe to store the summary statistics calculated from the OBIS records.

```{r Set up summary dataframe}
summary_df_list_nf<-list() #make a list to store each dataframe for each taxon
summary_cols_nf<- c("Species",	# These the columns that we want to calculate from OBIS
                   "n_occurrences",	
                   #Latitude
                   "min_latitude",
                   "average_latitude",
                   "median_latitude",
                   "max_latitude",
                   "latitude_stderr",
                   "lat_10thpct",
	                 "lat_90thpct",
                   
                   #Longitude
	                 "max_longitude",
	                 "min_longitude",
	                 "long_10thpct",
	                 "long_90thpct",
                   
                   #Depth
	                 "minimum_depth",	
	                 "average_depth",
	                 "median_depth",
	                 "maximum_depth",
                   "depth_stderr",
                   
                   #Salinity
	                 "minimum_salinity",
	                 "average_salinity",
	                 "median_salinity",
	                 "maximum_salinity",
                   "salinity_stderr",
                   
                   #SST
	                 "minimum_sst",
	                 "average_sst",
	                 "median_sst",
	                 "maximum_sst",
                   "sst_stderr")

summary_df_nf<- data.frame(matrix(nrow = 0, ncol = length(summary_cols_nf))) # empty dataframe
colnames(summary_df_nf)<- summary_cols_nf #assigning column names

```

## Pulling data from OBIS
Filtering but with specified geographic area and nonfossil records
```{r}
# Iterate through taxa list that we know are in OBIS and in our samples
for (i in seq_len(nrow(obis_taxa_df))){
  taxa<- obis_taxa_list[[i]]
  occ<-occurrence(scientificname=taxa,
                  hasextensions = "basisOfRecord", #make sure this field is included to check for fossil vs. nonfossil
                  geometry= obis_w_atl #Western Atlantic
                     )
  if (("decimalLatitude" %in% names(occ)) & ("decimalLongitude" %in% names(occ)) & ("bathymetry" %in% names(occ)) & ("sss" %in% names(occ)) & ("sst" %in% names(occ))){# Make sure we have these columns to calculate our environmental stats
   if (nrow(occ) !=0){ #make sure record isn't empty
    filt_occ<- occ[(occ$scientificName == taxa) & #making sure fields aren't empty/NA
                              (occ$basisOfRecord != "FossilSpecimen") & #not fossil
                              (!is.na(occ$bathymetry)) &
                              (!is.na(occ$decimalLatitude)) &
                              (!is.na(occ$decimalLongitude)) &
                              (!is.na(occ$sss)) &
                              (!is.na(occ$sst)) & 
                     (occ$bathymetry >=0), #not on land
                            ]

    n_occs<- nrow(filt_occ) # calculating number of occurrences
    
    if (nrow(filt_occ != 0)){ #if there is still data post-filtering, then calculate the following
      #latitude stats (min, max, mean, median, standard error, 10th and 90th percentile)
      min_lat<- min(filt_occ$decimalLatitude)
      max_lat<- max(filt_occ$decimalLatitude)
      avg_lat<- mean(filt_occ$decimalLatitude)
      med_lat<- median(filt_occ$decimalLatitude)
      lat_se<- std.error(filt_occ$decimalLatitude)
      
      lat_10th<- quantile(filt_occ$decimalLatitude, 0.1)
      lat_90th<- quantile(filt_occ$decimalLatitude, 0.9)
      
      #longitude stats (min, max, 10th and 90th percentile)
      max_long<- max(filt_occ$decimalLongitude)
      min_long<- min(filt_occ$decimalLongitude)
      long_10th<- quantile(filt_occ$decimalLongitude, 0.1)
      long_90th<- quantile(filt_occ$decimalLongitude, 0.9)
      
      #depth stats (min, max, median, mean, standard error)
      min_depth <- min(filt_occ$bathymetry)
      avg_depth<- mean(filt_occ$bathymetry)
      med_depth<- median(filt_occ$bathymetry)
      max_depth<- max(filt_occ$bathymetry)
      depth_se <- std.error(filt_occ$bathymetry)
      
      #salinity stats (min, max, median, mean, standard error)
      min_salinity<- min(filt_occ$sss)
      avg_salinity<- mean(filt_occ$sss)
      med_salinity<- median(filt_occ$sss)
      max_salinity<- max(filt_occ$sss)
      salinity_se<- std.error(filt_occ$sss)
      
      #sea surface temp stats (min, max, median, mean, standard error)
      min_sst <- min(filt_occ$sst)
      avg_sst<- mean(filt_occ$sst)
      med_sst<- median(filt_occ$sst)
      max_sst<- max(filt_occ$sst)
      sst_se<- std.error(filt_occ$sst)
      
      # make a summary dataframe for each taxon, with a column for each stat
      taxa_summary_nf<- data.frame(Species=c(taxa),
                                   n_occurences= c(n_occs),
                                   #lat stats
                                   min_latitude= c(min_lat),
                                   average_latitude= c(avg_lat),
                                   median_latitude = c(med_lat),
                                   max_latitude= c(max_lat),
                                   latitude_stderr= c(lat_se),
                                  
                                   lat_10thpct= c(lat_10th),
                                   lat_90thpct= c(lat_90th),
                                   #long stats
                                   max_longitude =c(max_long),
                                   min_longitude= c(min_long),
                                   long_10thpct =c(long_10th),
                                   long_90thpct= c(long_90th),
                                   
                                   #depth stats
                                   minimum_depth= c(min_depth),
                                   average_depth= c(avg_depth),
                                   median_depth= c(med_depth),
                                   maximum_depth= c(max_depth),
                                   depth_stderr= c(depth_se),
                                   
                                   #salinity stats
                                   minimum_salinity = c(min_salinity),
                                   average_salinity= c(avg_salinity),
                                   median_salinity=c(med_salinity),
                                   maximum_salinity= c(max_salinity),
                                   salinity_stderr= c(salinity_se),
                                   
                                   #sst stats
                                   minimum_sst= c(min_sst),
                                   average_sst= c(avg_sst),
                                   median_sst= c(med_sst),
                                   maximum_sst=c(max_sst),
                                   sst_sdterr= c(sst_se)
                                                    )
      summary_df_list_nf[[i]]<- taxa_summary_nf #add that taxon's summary table to the list of summary dataframes
      print(taxa)  
      }
     }
  }
}
    
```

## Output processing

Consolidating each taxon's environmental data into 1 dataframe
```{r}
all_taxa_summary_nf<- do.call(rbind, summary_df_list_nf) #bind all the taxon summary dataframes into one dataframe

all_taxa_summary_nf$taxon_name= all_taxa_summary_nf$Species #Assign the "taxon_name" column
```

Exporting
```{r}
all_tax_skrl_num= merge( all_taxa_summary_nf, taxa_df_raw, by="taxon_name") #merging with out original taxa list to preserve the our number system

write_csv(all_tax_skrl_num, "sp_env09272026.csv") #exporting as .csv
```
